subclassFeature.name: Conjurer
entries: {@i Step Across Space and Call Creatures from Thin Air}

A Conjurer considers distance and matter to be flexible guidelines rather than physical laws. Conjurers master magic that moves creatures instantly through space and summons creatures to fight on their behalf.

subclassFeature.name: Benign Transposition
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that you can see. Alternatively, you can choose a space within range that is occupied by a Medium or smaller creature. If that creature is willing, you both teleport, swapping places.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Conjuration Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Conjuration school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=C}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Conjuration school|spells|class=Wizard|school=C} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Distant Transposition
entries: The range of your Benign Transposition feature increases to 60 feet. Additionally, you can restore one use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Durable Summons
entries: When you cast a {@filter Conjuration spell|spells|school=C} to summon or create a creature using a spell slot, that creature gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Wizard level when it first appears. While it has these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to every damage type except Force, Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Conjuration
entries: Taking damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} on {@filter Conjuration spells|spells|school=C}.

subclassFeature.name: Splintered Summons
entries: When you use a spell slot to cast a {@filter Conjuration spell|spells|school=C} that summons a spirit whose stat block is included in the spell description, such as {@spell Summon Aberration|XPHB}, you can modify the spell to summon two creatures with the spell instead of one. Each creature is of the same kind, uses the stat block and rules denoted by the spell, and manifests in a different unoccupied space of your choice within the spell's range, but the summoned creatures' {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximums and current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are halved. If you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the spell, both creatures disappear.

Once you use this feature to modify a spell in this way, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Enchanter
entries: {@i Entrance and Beguile Others}
An Enchanter's magic clouds or captivates minds. Some Enchanters use their abilities to encourage peace and soften cruelty, while others use their mind-altering magic for selfish ends.

subclassFeature.name: Enchanting Conversationalist
entries: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}.
In addition, when you make an ability check with the chosen skill, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

subclassFeature.name: Enchantment Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Enchantment school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=E}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Enchantment school|spells|class=Wizard|school=E} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Hypnotic Presence
entries: Your charming words and enchanting gaze can enthrall another creature. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, choose one creature that you can see within 10 feet of yourself. If the target can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute or until the target is more than 10 feet away from you, the target can neither see nor hear you, or the target takes damage. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Split Enchantment
entries: When you use a spell slot to cast an {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E}, such as {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot to target an additional creature, you can increase the spell's effective level by 1.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Instinctive Charm
entries: When a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attack misses instead, and if there is another creature within range of the attack other than the attacker, the attacker targets that creature with the triggering attack, using the same attack roll. If multiple creatures are within the attack's range, you choose which one to target.

Once you take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by casting an {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E} with a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Alter Memories
entries: You can make a creature unaware of your magical influence. When you cast an {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E} that imposes the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition using a spell slot, you can choose one creature targeted by the spell. That creature remains unaware of being {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you.

In addition, once before the spell ends, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to force the chosen creature to make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can make the creature lose a number of hours of its memories equal to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 hour lost). You can make the creature forget less time, and the amount of time can't exceed the duration of your {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E}.

subclassFeature.name: Necromancer
entries: {@i Command the Powers of Death and Undeath}

You explore the forces of life, death, and undeath. As a necromancer, you learn to manipulate the energy that animates all creatures, and you draw increasing power from the forbidden secrets in your spellbook. Though many see Necromancers as menacing or villainous, not all Necromancers are evil.

subclassFeature.name: Necromancy Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Necromancy school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=N}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Necromancy school|spells|class=Wizard|school=N} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Necromancy Spellbook
entries: Your spellbook's necromantic secrets grant you additional powers. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Necrotic Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Undead Familiar
entries: The {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell appears in your spellbook. When you cast the spell, you choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: {@creature Skeleton|XMM} or {@creature Zombie|XMM} (see appendix B of the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB|11} for the familiar's stat block). When you choose one of the normal forms, you can choose Undead as its creature type.
Additionally, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

entries.name: Undead Vitality
entries: When you cast a {@filter Necromancy spell|spells|school=N} using a spell slot, you can choose an Undead creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the level of the spell slot expended plus your Wizard level.

subclassFeature.name: Grave Power
entries: You have discovered more necromantic insights and inscribed them in your spellbook. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Grave Resilience
entries: When you use Arcane Recovery, your {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, if any, decreases by 1.

entries.name: Overwhelming Necrosis
entries: Damage from your Wizard spells and Wizard features ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Undead Thralls
entries: You always have {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} prepared and can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can cast it in this way again. Whenever you start casting the spell, you can increase the spell's effective level by 1.
In addition, while holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: Whenever you cast a {@filter Necromancy spell|spells|school=N} that creates or summons an Undead, the Undead's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum and current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} increase by a number equal to your Intelligence modifier plus half your Wizard level (round down).

entries.name: Withering Strike
entries: Whenever an Undead you control within 60 feet of you hits a creature with an attack roll, the Undead deals extra Necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 Necrotic damage).

subclassFeature.name: Harvest Undead
entries: You have learned more secrets about the nuances of life and death. Immediately after you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB} but aren't reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from taking damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce an Undead creature under your control that you can see to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. You then immediately regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wizard level.

subclassFeature.name: Death's Master
entries: Abstruse rituals within your spellbook allow you mastery over undeath. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Bolster Undead
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose any number of Undead you have created or summoned with a {@filter Necromancy spell|spells|school=N} that are within 60 feet of you. Those Undead each gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wizard level. Once you use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Extinguish Undead
entries: When an Undead creature you can see is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can cause it to explode with necrotic energy. Roll a number of d6s equal to half the creature's unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} (round up, minimum of {@dice 1d6}), and add them together. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the Undead makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled and can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only. When you use this feature to explode an Undead creature you don't control, you must take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend a level 5+ spell slot to do so.

subclassFeature.name: Transmuter
entries: {@i Transform Energy and Matter}
You study spells that modify energy and matter—to you, the world is eminently mutable. Using your magic, you become a smith at reality's forge.
Some Transmuters are tinkerers and pranksters. Others seek the power to make and destroy worlds.

subclassFeature.name: Transmutation Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Transmutation school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=T}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one {@filter Wizard spell from the Transmutation school|spells|class=Wizard|school=T} to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Transmuter's Stone
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can create a magic stone that lasts until you use this feature again. The stone is a Tiny object, and you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Wizard spells. A creature with the stone in its possession gains proficiency in Constitution saving throws and one of the following benefits, which you choose when you create the stone. You can change the stone's benefit when you cast a {@filter Transmutation spell|spells|school=T} using a spell slot.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: The bearer gains {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet or increases the range of its {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} by 60 feet.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: The bearer gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage (your choice each time you choose this benefit).

entries.name: Speed
entries: The bearer's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Wondrous Alteration
entries: You always have the {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} spell prepared and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
While under the effects of {@spell Alter Self|XPHB}, you gain an additional benefit for each of its options.

entries.name: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: While underwater, you can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Change Appearance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Natural Weapons
entries: The damage of your new growth increases to {@dice 2d6} damage of the type associated with the growth. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Empowered Transmutation
entries: When you use a spell slot to cast a {@filter Transmutation spell|spells|school=T} that doesn't make an attack roll or force a saving throw, such as {@spell Fly|XPHB} or {@spell Magic Weapon|XPHB}, you can increase the spell's effective level by 1.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Stone
entries: Your Transmuter's Stone is more versatile. When you create your Transmuter's Stone, you can choose up to two benefits. You can choose each option other than {@b Resistance} only once. If you choose {@b Resistance} twice, you must choose different damage types. You can change either or both benefits when you cast a {@filter Transmutation spell|spells|school=T} using a spell slot.
In addition, the following are now among your benefit options for Transmuter's Stone.

entries.name: Mighty Build
entries: The bearer has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength saving throws. The bearer also counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity.

entries.name: Tremorsense
entries: The bearer gains {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Shape-Shifter
entries: You always have the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell prepared and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

In addition, when you target yourself with the spell, you can modify the spell to gain the benefits below. Once you modify the spell using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Game Statistics
entries: In addition to retaining the features specified in the spell, you retain your memories and ability to communicate. You also retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; proficiencies; class features; and feats.

entries.name: Transmute Spells
entries: While shape-shifted, you can cast spells, but only {@filter Transmutation spells|spells|school=T} that don't have a Material component that has a specified cost or that is consumed by the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Master Transmuter
entries: While you carry your Transmuter's Stone, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to consume the reserve of transmutation magic stored inside and choose one of the following benefits. After you use the stone in this way, it crumbles to dust. You can prevent the stone from crumbling by expending a level 7+ spell slot as part of the {@action Magic|XPHB} action you take using this feature.

entries.name: Major Transformation
entries: You can transmute one nonmagical object—no larger than a 10-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} or eight connected 5-foot Cubes—into another nonmagical object of similar size and mass and of equal or lesser value. You must spend 10 minutes handling the object to transform it.

entries.name: Panacea
entries: You touch a creature as part of this {@action Magic|XPHB} action, and the target regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum (round down). The target is cured of all magical contagions, and any curses affecting the target are lifted, including the target's {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to a cursed item. If the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} or {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition, those conditions end.

entries.name: Restore Life
entries: You cast the {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot, using the stone in place of the required Material components.

entries.name: Restore Youth
entries: You touch one willing creature as part of this {@action Magic|XPHB} action, and the target's {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, if any, decreases to 0, and it permanently appears {@dice 3d10} years younger, to a minimum of young adulthood.
